title: Volume 2 Chapter 2: The Sister Cries, the Flames Do Not, and the Dagger Remains Unbroken 1
content: It feels strange.
Shara Ransura, a church sister who had just recently belonged to the ordinary Healing Faction, licked the alcohol poured into a wooden mug — commonly known as Adventurer Alcohol.
The sharp sting pierced her tongue, and the intense alcohol assaulted not just her mouth but also her throat and insides.
From the name alone, it was clear that this drink was meant for adventurers; essentially, it was beer with increased alcohol content.
As long as it gets you drunk, that’s all that matters.
A drink aimed solely at getting you wasted has no regard for taste.
It’s definitely not something you drink with the intention of enjoying.
Having reached this conclusion quickly, Shara set the mug back down on the table.
Right now, she was being dragged into a "celebration for defeating the Forest Dragon!" by Shin and Erika.
She knew that her colleagues in the Demon Subjugation Faction, who didn’t have the strength to fight alongside adventurers, would often drink with them after slaying monsters.
She was aware of this, but what she knew was far more subdued.

Looking at the adventurers who were showcasing their party tricks by tearing apart their upper body gear — Shara knew that adventurers’ equipment was often expensive because it was tied to their lives — she thought, Are these guys idiots?
Oh, there was no room for doubt there.
It was odd, truly odd.
"Shall we celebrate?" she had indeed asked Shin.
She had invited him out of a faint longing for the kind of celebration that the Demon Subjugation Faction held after finishing a job with adventurers...
And this was the result.
Well, it seems Shara understands a little.
That’s when Shin began to call out to the adventurers who participated in this ruckus, and that was the start of all the mistakes.
The adventurer named Barel, who was called out by Shin, looked incredibly annoyed.
Of course. There were too many people. Just securing a place that could accommodate everyone would be a job in itself.
Shara certainly didn’t want a celebration with such a large crowd.
All she hoped for was to enjoy a nice meal at a somewhat fancy place.
She definitely did not want to see a muscular man turning red-faced while trying to tear his own clothes apart without using his hands as a party trick.
Since the clothes couldn’t be reused, it was literally a one-time performance.
What an idiot!
I don’t want to see that!
Shave your chest hair!
Barel, the adventurer, was also an adventurer. If he thought it was annoying, he should have just declined properly.
What do you mean,
"It can’t be helped, it’s Longdagger’s invitation
There’s nothing unavoidable about this!
Where was the unavoidable part?
The man inviting you to celebrate is a fool trying to impress his wife in front of a dragon the size of a castle!
You shouldn’t just say
"It can’t be helped
" to such a fool!
…Well, maybe it could be a little unavoidable. It’s a bit hard to understand.
Shara picked up the mug again and took a sip.
It still tasted like stupidity.
Yes, that’s exactly it.
Shara thought. Those two are not normal.
No, it was clear from the start that they weren’t normal. After all, they had easily defeated the Golden Ogre.
Moreover, they casually donated most of the reward to the orphanage.
It didn’t make sense. Certainly, the orphanage in Hekatai wasn’t unrelated to adventurers.
Many of the children taken in by the orphanage were the offspring of adventurers. Adventurers die easily.
This is an undeniable fact.
Because of that, the orphanage in Hekatai receives many donations from adventurers.
Because they have friends’ children, because they come from the orphanage, because they don’t know when they might die.
But even so, there are no adventurers who would casually donate that amount.
At first, Shara was surprised by that amount and moved by the nobility of the Longdagger couple.
But now she understood.
Those two are just crazy.
When she was handed half of the reward for defeating the Forest Dragon, Shara was convinced.
Receiving an outrageous sum of money, she honestly didn’t understand and went crying to the bishop.
For Shara, the bishop of the Makikomaru Church was a father figure, a respected mentor, and someone who had entrusted her to those two.
She felt she had the right to cry to him, so she did so without holding back.
She thought she wasn’t mistaken when she saw the bishop’s usually gentle smile twitch slightly.
Which of those two made his face twitch?
Was it because of the amount of the donation he was handed again?
Or was it because they had defeated a dragon the size of a castle?
Either way, Shara thought.
She didn’t want this kind of celebration.
Seeing the idiot who suddenly appeared trying to rip his clothes apart on the table made her sigh.
No, no, no.
She remembered that what she had been feeling strange about wasn’t because of the muscular idiot trying to tear apart his clothes.
The problem lay with the two of them, Shin and Erika.
These two, Shara realized, were a bit too far from normal.
She thought it was too late to realize this, but during the last incident with the castle-like Forest Dragon, everything had ended before her head could catch up.
To be precise, she hadn’t seen what had happened because she was busy preparing to escape with Erika in her arms, turning her back to the dragon.
Thinking back, how could I have turned my back to that huge dragon?
Shara shook her head in surprise at her unexpected boldness.
Perhaps it was the alcohol that was derailing her thoughts.
Through this commotion, Shara finally realized.
The strength of Shin and Erika, who had defeated the third Forest Dragon, was "a bit" beyond common sense.
Even a novice sister from the Demon Subjugation Faction could think that.
That was definitely dangerous.
Shara shivered at the memory.
There were many adventurers around.
So, the two of them relentlessly sliced apart the Forest Dragon, which kept reviving annoyingly.
Using a sword technique that clearly cut something longer than the length of the sword, Erika restrained the dragon’s movements.
Even so, Shin knocked down the dragon that was still rampaging.
Perhaps due to the third battle, or perhaps they had just gotten used to it. Though it took time, it was one-sided.
It didn’t make sense; undoubtedly, everyone else felt the same way.
Shara didn’t miss the expressions of the adventurers who had initially tried to assist but quickly turned pale in just a few moments.
Aren’t you amazing? That’s the adventurer I’m going on adventures with! Why is it me?
With her head starting to spin from the alcohol, Shara pondered.
Why is it me? Why am I the one, Bishop?
She recalled the bishop’s face when he told her to act alongside Shin and the others.
Since it had come with an order to change factions, she hadn’t had time to feel shocked or question it back then.
But why was it her?
Today, Shara felt acutely aware that she couldn’t be of any help to those two.
When members of the church are dispatched to adventurers, the role they are generally expected to fulfill is that of a user of Healing Magic.
But she couldn’t fulfill that role.
No, it wasn’t that she couldn’t do it, but those two were clearly better at Healing Magic than she was.
As for Shin, he was the kind of healer who made you want to ask,
"Are you secretly a dragon or something?
In that case, her expected role would be as an attacker using offensive magic, but Erika was too versatile and excellent for that as well.
There was no place for her to step in.
Sure, she had dealt significant damage to the first Forest Dragon with her destructive magic, but that was merely a convenient time-saving measure.
Even that would fall short if Erika didn’t care about the surrounding damage.
It didn’t make sense; it seriously didn’t make sense.
Dragons are not something you just beat to death. In fact, you shouldn’t beat them to death.
Shin and the others seemed to have come from abroad, but Shara wondered which country would let go of those two.
At the very least, if they were to leave the Makikomaru territory, they would be held back at all costs.
Those two were that exceptional.
And why was she the one paired with them...?
As she sipped the Adventurer Alcohol that she had only been tasting little by little, Shara found herself tilting her head.
When I get back, I’ll ask the bishop why it’s me.
Yesterday, she had fallen asleep from the fatigue of the Forest Dragon subjugation, and today, she hadn’t had the chance to talk leisurely due to the idiots crowding the church since morning.
She had no shortage of complaints to share.
Bishop, I did my best too, you know?
Did you know those two were that powerful?
Please listen to me, Bishop!
Shara murmured with her fuzzy head.
What a terrible celebration.
I thought, as I looked at the group of idiots sprawled over a hastily set-up table on the street due to a lack of seats, snoring away.
The noise was somewhat tolerable only for the first thirty minutes or so.
When adventurers get half-drunk, they start using body enhancement magic in their drunken state, leading to casualties.
To prevent that, the alcohol served to adventurers is generally high in alcohol content.
And the idiots don’t have the option of not drinking.
As a result, the weak-drinking idiots quickly pass out, while the strong-drinking idiots can’t properly use their body enhancement.
It’s quite well thought out, but honestly, that was a bit harsh.
When Shara said she wanted to celebrate, I called out to Barel, but I never expected everyone to tag along!
We rented out three taverns near the Adventurer Guild,
"spanning
" across them, and celebrated in a very adventurer-like manner.
In other words, we drank, ate, and sang.
Fortunately, there were no idiots who started dancing, but it probably wasn’t much of a fortune for the tavern owners who were suddenly caught up in this.
Also, the wise adventurers who didn’t drink were having a tough time.
There’s nothing more difficult than collecting money from drunken idiots.
Poor them, pretending to be smart in a crowd of idiots is bound to lead to trouble.
After all, there are only idiots among adventurers.
Erika and I, steeped in noble habits, enjoyed our drinks while recovering from drunkenness with Healing Magic, so we didn’t embarrass ourselves.
We completely ignored the people looking at us with pleading eyes.
Well, because we’re nobles, we don’t really understand money matters.
Well, I did embarrass myself when one drunken idiot tried to casually throw his arm around Erika’s shoulder, so forgive me for not being the smart one.
The idiot I sent flying should understand that I was just trying to enjoy a nice drink with Erika, and that his dirty chest hair got cleaned up nicely.
For some reason, while a series of idiots kept challenging me, Erika seemed to be having a good time chatting with the female adventurers, so she probably didn’t see anything embarrassing.
"That was fun."
All things considered, it was quite enjoyable.
Since I had basically been active solo in Faltarl, I had a bit of a longing for the kind of celebration adventurers have after finishing a job together.
"Yes, it was fun. The reckless drinking without a thought for tomorrow was truly adventurer-like."
Even nobles enjoy getting drunk, even if they use Healing Magic to recover from it.
Therefore, nobles know how to leave just the right amount of drunkenness.
Especially the upper-class nobles are skilled at it.
With her cheeks slightly flushed, Erika let out a small sigh-like breath while smiling.
By the way, lower-class nobles either get completely wasted or quickly sober up for tomorrow’s work.
Serving at the palace is tough.
Hang in there, Father.
Shin, you’re tearing the chest hair off idiots, and the idiots are starting to strip.
This isn’t the kind of celebration I wanted!
What I had heard from my seniors wasn’t anything like this! Give me back my dreams!
The sister, who was bad at Healing Magic, protested with a bright red face.
It’s wrong to have a longing for what adventurers do.
"That’s true. Next time, let’s just have the three of us."
I nodded in agreement.
This time, it was because we, the newcomers, suddenly stood out by earning money.
It also served as a face show and a greeting.
What kind of clever-sounding thing are you saying?
In what world do idiots tear off chest hair as a greeting?
Don’t be ridiculous.
This girl.
It’s important, you know? A newcomer’s greeting.
It can’t be helped, right?
He tried to touch my wife in front of me!
Just being attached to her body is already a kindness.
Well, I understand the desire to touch something beautiful.
Pya.
Erika let out a cute hiccup.
"There’s no way that’s acceptable! Are you an idiot? You’re an idiot!"
Shara raised both hands in protest, and for some reason, I envisioned a hamster.
"I get it, I get it. As an apology, I’ll give you something nice, so hold out your hand."
"Is it candy?"
What are you, a child?
Thinking that, I placed a leather pouch on Shara’s palm.
"Whoa! Huh?!"
Shara was momentarily surprised by the weight of the leather pouch, her expression turning serious as if she had forgotten her drunkenness.
"Could it be?"
As she asked cautiously, I smiled and nodded back.
"This is the reward from this time."
Shara let out a scream.
Poor thing, she walked home cautiously, wary of every corner.
She could use enough body enhancement to keep up with us, so even if she had a bit of a hangover, she shouldn’t fall behind thieves.
Well, I was the one who forcibly handed her a large sum of money that she didn’t want.
Watching her walk away nervously, I couldn’t help but sigh.
I don’t want to doubt her, but...
"Erika, what do you think?"
"What about? More importantly, who are you talking about?"
As we watched Shara’s retreating figure, Erika responded to me.
Her eyes, slightly glazed from the alcohol, were gently narrowed.
Just that alone allowed me to gauge her feelings.
The fact that Erika was making such a face meant she had taken a liking to Shara.
So I hesitated to say the next words.
I felt guilty about making Erika feel unpleasant.
"I heard Shara let slip some words that she didn’t mean to say. Did you hear them, Erika?"
Erika nodded with a smile at my question.
It had happened during the battle against the Forest Dragon.
While Erika and I were beating up the Forest Dragon, trying not to involve other adventurers, Shara had let slip something like this.
"I never imagined they had such strength. I must report this to the bishop."
Whether it was because she had let her guard down since we were in the middle of a battle or if it was a genuine slip of the tongue, I had picked up exactly what Shara said with my enhanced hearing.
Erika, whose hearing was also enhanced by body enhancement, must have heard it too.
It was hard to believe that I heard it and Erika missed it.
Moreover, the drunken Shara had been mumbling similar things at the tavern.
She must have gotten too drunk on the unfamiliar Adventurer Alcohol.
She had been going on about how she needed to tell the bishop or confront them.
Thinking back, it had been odd from the start.
Sending a sister from the church to a pair of adventurers who had defeated three Golden Ogres, even if they were Rank 1.
For adventurers to be sent by the church, they would typically be of a master class, and moreover, the sister sent would be expected to possess corresponding strength.
While our own ranks were one thing, Shara’s own strength could only be described as insufficient for a sister being dispatched.
Though her ability to cast spells at that speed was impressive, her Healing Magic was far too poor for someone from the church.
From both the perspective of those being dispatched and those dispatching, it would appear as though she was lacking in strength.
While adventurer ranks are merely decorations for adventurers, they are not so for outsiders.
That leads to one conclusion.
Shara is a spy sent by the church to monitor Erika.
If that’s the case, it would make sense of what Shara let slip.
Shara would have been monitoring Erika under the bishop’s orders.
If it were a bishop class, they would likely know that Erika is Erika Solnzali.
And they would also know why Erika, a noble from another country, is in Hekatai.

Speaking of which, when Shara mentioned something about informing the bishop regarding the donation, it was likely because she understood the basic principle of mixing truth into lies to make the lies believable.
Though her impression might be that Shara couldn’t pull off such cunning, she had completely deceived me.
If she hadn’t let those words slip, I might not have realized it even now.
Despite having thought that I needed to be cautious around church-related people, here I was.
Sighing at my own incompetence, I said to Erika.
"If you heard that murmur, then it’s quick work. I think Shara is likely monitoring you under the bishop’s orders."
Yes, that seems reasonable.
The church should consider it fortunate that they are not being targeted for their lives, as they are considered enemies of God.
Erika’s face, which she said with a hint of sarcasm, didn’t seem particularly worried.
And she didn’t appear disappointed either.
Having seen Erika and Shara enjoying their conversation, I thought Erika might feel hurt upon discovering that Shara was a spy from the church.
It seemed Erika’s heart was much stronger than I had imagined.
"I don’t particularly mind being monitored, you know? Shara is a fun person."
From that remark, it was clear that Erika liked Shara, regardless of the monitoring.
To be honest, I didn’t dislike Shara as an individual; on the contrary, I found her quite likable.
Her spirit of risking her life just to buy time to save villagers, even while severely injured, was admirable.
She might be a bit noisy, but her noisiness brought a smile to Erika’s face, so it was within the acceptable range.
However...
"What if the church is targeting your assassination?"
I noticed my face darkening as I said that.
Erika’s response to my question was silence.
She gently placed her hand on her well-shaped chin, looking down in thought.
"I’m surprised."
"What surprised you?"
"That I hadn’t considered that possibility."
Erika waved for me to follow her as she began to walk through the night streets.
Once she confirmed that I was following, Erika continued speaking.
"However, that seems like a bit of a leap in reasoning, doesn’t it?"
Is that so?
From their perspective, you are...
As you said, it’s only natural for you to be considered an enemy of God.
At my words, Erika shrugged lightly.
Yes, that’s certainly true.
But even so, there are ways to go about it.
You remember, the one who targeted my life turned into a demon, right?
That’s not exactly a method the church would typically use.
Demons, as the church calls them, are beings without divine protection.
The church claims that creatures who lose their divine protection become demons.
Where demons originate from is still a mystery, so everyone somewhat believes this theory.
But there’s no evidence.
Demons appear suddenly, wreak havoc without purpose, and are then subjugated.
That’s all we know for sure.
We were attacked by assassins shortly after departing Faltarl.
I still can’t believe it, but during that time, one of the assassins transformed into a demon.
For the church to use such beings, well, that certainly seems uncharacteristic of them.
However...
"If there’s a possibility, I won’t dismiss that thought."
As I said this while gazing into Erika’s eyes, she wore a slightly exasperated yet pleased expression.
I can tell you’re genuinely concerned for me, but if you think too much, those wrinkles on your forehead won’t go away.
Seeing me instinctively touch my forehead, Erika laughed.
Regardless of what the church or the bishop thinks, for now, we can only observe, so there’s no need to deepen those wrinkles, my dear.
Bival Bivality, the bishop of Hekatai, was in a modest room contemplating Shara.
He thought of her as a poor girl.
The experience of having to change factions from the Healing Faction to the Demon Subjugation Faction was a painful one.
Bishop Bival knew this well.
He had gone through the same experience himself.
In his youth, Bishop Bival had aimed to heal people as a member of the Healing Faction.
However, like Shara, he had been poor at Healing Magic.
No matter how much he trained in magic, he only excelled at offensive magic.
When he was told to move to the Demon Subjugation Faction by the faction’s heavyweights, he felt sadness and regret.
Thus, Bishop Bival understood Shara’s feelings well.
Though he had never gone so far as to engage in the bizarre behavior of mastering offensive magic while still identifying as a member of the Healing Faction.
Why did that girl try to learn casting magic? No, really, why?
Bishop Bival’s evaluation of Shara was that she was a bit odd, but it was true that he was concerned for her well-being and future.
That’s why he decided to entrust Shara to the adventurers known as the Longdagger couple.
Their ability to defeat three Golden Ogres without a scratch, and their spirit of donating most of the money earned from that subjugation to the orphanage.
There couldn’t be more suitable adventurers for sending Shara.
Of course, he knew that one half of that couple was Erika Solnzali, but Bishop Bival didn’t see that as a problem.
Rather, he didn’t even believe the allegations against Erika Solnzali.
After all, she was from the Solnzali family.
There was no way someone from that family would do anything that would indirectly harm orphans.
Bishop Bival was aware of his own ignorance of worldly politics, yet he had seen many strange power struggles within the noble society.
He concluded that this was likely the same.
If it were a story about another noble family, he might have thought that there could be foolish nobles who would consider harming the Maiden of Light.
As he listened to the noisy footsteps approaching down the hallway, he smiled, wondering what kind of story that girl would tell him today.
The next day.
When Erika suggested going out for another subjugation, I had to convince her that her torn equipment was not suitable for going out.
The extent of the damage was so severe that it was beyond what an amateur could handle.
"Well, it can’t be helped. Sending my husband in such a pitiful state isn’t something a lady would do."
It was because she had taken damage severe enough to tear her clothes, but I thought it was typical of Erika to say she couldn’t let him go out in torn clothes.
But adventurers’ equipment isn’t exactly a death shroud, you know?
However, buying new equipment.
The frugality instilled in me from being born into a poor viscount family was bubbling up, but since it had only lasted a day after being repaired, it was probably at its limit.
I think, in the Faltarl Kingdom, I had been mending my own clothes until the last moment.

Since I had the money from selling the Forest Dragon’s magic stone, I didn’t need to worry about finances, but if I used it carelessly, it would quickly run out, which is a common story among adventurers.
Equipment for adventurers is notoriously expensive.
In the past, I had worn my gear down to the last thread, much to the astonishment of my friends, but now Erika was by my side.
Standing next to her in patched-up clothes would be worth a death sentence.
What if she ended up disliking me? Men’s clothes are changed based on women’s tastes.
So, I went to the armor shop, the one with that slightly eccentric shopkeeper, to gather equipment, and while Erika and I were having a slightly late lunch at the dining hall, it happened.
